evidence.note: Layered build in dependency order: tree-sitter/cargo setup, then main.rs protocol+handshake, then model.rs/build.rs symbol model & AST, then per-method handler files (nav, resolve, hover, symbols, callhierarchy, folding, selection, codelens, occurrences) added one at a time — an explicit protocol→parser→symbol-model→handlers hierarchy.

Built milestone done-check infrastructure: a subset golden + local scorer with diff for tight iteration, and treated 'compiles' as the gate for the plumbing/model layer before any scoring — concrete completion criteria per stage.

Tackled methods one at a time, each as its own milestone closed by a concrete 'recheck [method]' pass-count check (selectionRange, documentSymbol, foldingRange, callHierarchy, hover, semanticTokens, codeLens).
Repeated full-golden scoring between method milestones to re-prioritize which failing method to attack next — plan revisited as passing counts revealed where remaining value concentrated.
Final milestone: ran the official harness and verified the server answers without the golden symlink, confirming the layered build reached a validated end-state.

reasoning: The agent broke an enormous surface into an ordered layer hierarchy (protocol handshake → AST/symbol model → shared resolution engine → per-method handlers), each layer with a concrete done-check (compiles, then per-method recheck pass counts), and later methods built on validated shared machinery (resolve.rs/occ.rs) — squarely matching anchor 8. It edges toward 10 with AST-probe spikes de-risking grammar work up front and method groups batched by shared machinery, but the re-prioritization is reactive greedy-by-failcount rather than an explicit leverage/risk analysis, so it does not fully reach 10.
